title: Enterprise reservation negotiation playbook: preemption windows, grace-band overage credits, and autoscale gating
creator: Lena Ortiz
description:
Context: Enterprise procurement often requests reserved GPU commitments but also needs flexibility for burst and unpredictable usage. Current offerings (flat reserved bands + ad-hoc bursts) surface negotiation friction: customers want predictable cost ceilings, contractual preemption guarantees, and clear mechanisms for overage smoothing during peak events.

Goal: Create a negotiation playbook and experimental pricing constructs that combine: (1) defined preemption windows for elastic capacity, (2) a 'grace-band' of overage credits that smooths billing during short spikes, and (3) autoscale gating rules that tie SLA tiers to burst allowances. This playbook will be used by sales and solutions to close enterprise Dedicated commitments with transparent economic and operational terms.

Success metrics: (a) 20% reduction in deal negotiation cycle time for Dedicated contracts > $200k ARR, (b) 10% increase in conversion rate for flexible-commit pilots, (c) <5 disputes/month on overage billing for pilots during the 90-day experiment window.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Documented playbook with 3 recommended pricing constructs (strict reserve, reserve+grace, cushion credits) and corresponding legal clause templates. 2) Worked examples (3 customer archetypes) with modeled P&L impact. 3) Internal training doc + one-pager for sales + decision matrix for sizing preemption windows. 4) Pilot terms ready for legal and finance signoff.
deliverables:
- Playbook PDF (sales+legal)
- 3 example pricing models with spreadsheet scenarios
- Contract clause language snippets for SQ/CX teams
- Sales one-pager and negotiation checklist
- Pilot offer template for initial customers
risks: Operational complexity in autoscale gating leading to SLA regressions
notes:
Key trade-offs discussed in scoping: longer preemption windows reduce capacity fragmentation but weaken guaranteed throughput; grace-band credits improve commercial cadence but add billing complexity; autoscale gating needs tight integration with runtime telemetry to avoid false triggers.

We plan to rely on runtime-1.20 autoscale telemetry hooks (ENG-19821) and billing back-end experiments (PM-49987) to implement metering for grace credits.
